History and Perspectives: Wilhelm Wundt
Founder of the first psychology laboratory in 1879
Introspection
Early method of examining and reporting one's own conscious experience
Structuralism
Approach analysing consciousness into its basic elements
Functionalism
Approach studying the purpose mental processes serve in adaptation
Behaviorism
Approach restricting psychology to observable behaviour
Psychodynamic perspective
View emphasising unconscious drives and early experience
Humanistic psychology
View emphasising free will, growth, and self-actualisation
Cognitive revolution
The mid-century return to studying internal mental processes
Evolutionary psychology
Explaining behaviour through natural selection pressures
Eclectic approach
Drawing on several perspectives rather than committing to one
Research Methods and Ethics: Operational definition
Defining a variable by exactly how it is measured
Random sampling
Selecting participants so every member has an equal chance
Random assignment
Placing participants into conditions by chance to control confounds
Confounding variable
An uncontrolled factor offering an alternative explanation
Experimental group
The group receiving the treatment being tested
Control group
The comparison group not receiving the treatment
Correlation coefficient
A number from -1 to 1 describing strength and direction of a relationship
Illusory correlation
Perceiving a relationship where none actually exists
Statistical significance
The likelihood a result is not due to chance alone
Replication
Repeating a study to see whether the finding holds
Informed consent
Participants agreeing with full knowledge of what is involved
Debriefing
Explaining a study's true nature to participants afterward
Institutional review board
The committee that approves research for ethical compliance
Hindsight bias
The tendency to see an outcome as obvious after learning it

Axon
The fibre carrying the signal away from the cell body
Resting potential
The neuron's baseline negative charge when inactive

A neuron either fires fully or not at all
Refractory period
The brief pause before a neuron can fire again

Antagonist drug
A drug that blocks a neurotransmitter's effect
Medulla

Cerebellum

Thalamus

Wernicke's area

The gland network releasing hormones into the bloodstream

Rules by which we organise elements into wholes

A mental grouping of similar objects or ideas
Prototype
The most typical example of a category

Crystallized intelligence

Reliability
